name: When is it worth converting an existing bathtub into a walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: When is it worth converting an existing bathtub into a walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A conversion is practical if you rarely use your bathtub or want safer, barrier-free access. Converting a tub requires removing the tub apron, reconfiguring the drain assembly from a standard 1.5-inch tub drain to a 2-inch shower drain to handle faster water flow, and rebuilding the wall envelope. If your household has only one full bathroom with a tub, removing it might affect resale appeal for future buyers with small children. However, for primary suites or homeowners prioritizing accessibility, replacing an awkward tub with a spacious walk-in shower significantly improves daily comfort and safety.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tub conversions are ideal for improved accessibility and daily convenience, provided your plumbing can be updated from a 1.5-inch tub drain to a 2-inch shower drain.
